title: Sonopet aspirates support genomic and epigenomic profiling of skull-base meningioma
summary: In a prospectively collected paired feasibility series of seven patients, Sonopet aspirate and standard-resection skull-base meningioma specimens produced comparable sequencing yield, read quality and tumor purity. Copy-number profiles were highly concordant (Lin’s CCC0.99;95% CI0.76–1.00), whereas somatic variant-burden agreement was weaker and imprecise (CCC0.53;95% CI−0.28–0.99); promoter methylation was closely correlated. Learned Dorado models interpreted nanopore sequence/modified-base signals, and the ClairS-TO neural ensemble called somatic variants for the comparison. This small specimen-feasibility study, partly funded by Stryker, does not establish improved patient outcomes or independent replication.
ai_technology: Dorado high-accuracy and modified-base models; ClairS-TO trained neural-network ensemble
organization: The University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center; Mayo Clinic

evidence.tested: Prospective paired specimen comparison in seven patients. Copy-number concordance CCC 0.99 (95% CI 0.76–1.00); somatic SNV burden CCC 0.53 (95% CI −0.28–0.99); promoter methylation reported as closely correlated.
evidence.unknown: Somatic-variant agreement has wide uncertainty in seven patients; intratumoral heterogeneity is a possible explanation, not established here. Prospective specimen collection is not prospective clinical-outcome validation; separate replication and patient benefit were not assessed in this series.
evidence.ai_role: Dorado learned models base-called genomic and methylation signal; ClairS-TO trained neural networks estimated somatic variants, enabling the comparison of aspirate and resection profiles.

source_review.scope: Publisher article abstract; paired-specimen Methods; Dorado and ClairS-TO bioinformatic Methods; concordance Results; affiliations and funding/competing-interest declaration. Supplementary file not reviewed.
